title: Sell Mineral Rights in Balmorhea, TX
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Balmorhea, TX | Royalty Buyer
metaDescription: Balmorhea sits on the southern edge of Reeves County's heavy Delaware Basin drilling. See how a former operations engineer prices minerals here.
heroLead: Most people know Balmorhea for the spring-fed swimming pool, but the ground around it sits within reach of some of Reeves County's most active drilling.
intro: Balmorhea is small, a few hundred residents at most, and it's easy to assume the mineral acreage around it doesn't matter much in the broader Delaware Basin story. That's not quite right. Reeves County as a whole has been one of the busiest counties for horizontal permitting in Texas, and acreage on the southern end of the county, including around Balmorhea, has seen its share of that activity, though generally less densely than the core near Pecos and Orla.

sections.heading: Southern Reeves County positioning
paragraphs: Balmorhea sits toward the edge of Reeves County's most heavily drilled acreage rather than dead center in it, which means I weigh current production data more heavily than speculative future drilling when I value an interest here, compared to how I'd approach acreage closer to the county's core.

sections.heading: What I need from you
paragraphs: A division order or recent royalty check stub is the fastest way to a real number. If your acreage hasn't produced yet, tell me the section and block and I'll check permitting activity for that specific area rather than assuming based on the town's location alone.

sections.heading: Small-town ownership, real value
paragraphs: A lot of ownership around Balmorhea traces to long-held family land, often split among heirs who've moved away over the years. The town being small doesn't mean the interest is small. I've bought interests here that surprised the owner once I showed them the actual production numbers behind their check.

sections.heading: How I actually build the offer
paragraphs: I pull the well or wells tied to your specific unit from Texas Railroad Commission records, look at where each sits on its decline curve, and check what's permitted nearby before I settle on a range. That process takes me a day or two once I have your division order, not weeks of back and forth.

faqs.question: Is Balmorhea in the busiest part of Reeves County's drilling?
faqs.answer: Not the busiest core, which sits more toward Pecos and Orla, but there's still real activity on the southern end of the county. I evaluate your specific tract rather than assuming based on the town.

faqs.question: My interest has never produced anything, is it worth anything?
faqs.answer: Possibly, depending on nearby permitting activity. Send me the location and I'll give you an honest read rather than a blanket yes or no.

faqs.question: How quickly can a small interest like this close?
faqs.answer: Typically three to six weeks once we have a signed agreement and title is confirmed clean, longer if there's unresolved probate to work through first.
